section.title: What Shepard Bought at Purgatory
section.form_description: A speech meant to move someone to act — the narrator talking Shepard (or whoever is listening) up off the floor and back into the fight. Sections are the rising beats of an address: the stakes named, the doubt named plainly, the evidence from a life lived that it can be done, the call. The narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it — but so is the listener's: the narrator holds up the other person's record as often as their own, since it's their record the speech is meant to land on.
section.form_note:
The brief is a speech, not a life story: Jack talking Shepard up in the last hour before the last push, using her own record as proof it can be done. Set after the Cerberus coup, the Citadel DLC shore leave, and the Cronos Station assault, this is the morning of the London conduit assault on Earth — everything is already staged (ships loaded, the plan set, the crew briefed), and the only thing left to do is get up and launch it. Jack is rousing Shepard right before he walks out to fight, not settling him in for the night. Romanced Jack per canon.choices (romance: Jack), consummated per jack_meeting/normandy-engineering scene at the end of ME2, with the Citadel DLC back tattoo. Note: choices.yaml's citadel_coup detail says Thane "died protecting the dalatrass," but the event record (thane-krios-death-defending-the-salarian-councilor) and the coup scene (citadel-coup-csec-office-kai-leng) both have him dying for the Salarian Councilor — treating this as the user's shorthand slip, not a real contradiction, and writing it as the Councilor. Per Thomas's request, "what-cerberus-made-me-for" and "the-kids-at-grissom" were rebuilt off shared Shepard/Jack history and broader lore instead of the Teltin and Grissom backstory events: recruitment off the Purgatory prison ship (jack-recruitment-purgatory) plus the Jack/Miranda confrontation Shepard settled (jack_miranda_dispute: appeased both), and the Suicide Mission itself (Jack held the biotic barrier, all-survived outcome per suicide_mission canon). Pragia/Teltin and Grissom get at most a glancing bridging mention, never the anchor. Jack's framing of "holding a barrier is a focus problem, not a strength problem" and "Cerberus bought a weapon and Shepard made a person" are her own editorializing on the record, not new corpus facts.
Revision per Thomas: Shepard's own AU record is now a load-bearing second thread, not a token mention. Jack is pitching HIM back to himself — every section now carries at least one beat where she cites something true of Shepard specifically as the proof, not just her own Purgatory/barrier/Brimstone/Murtock record. Sourced from config/canon/choices.yaml's Shepard AU overrides (Normandy-born, no parents, gang and drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7; Sole Survivor of Akuze, the whole squad dead but him; Vanguard, biotic charge into the guns; alignment "Paragon, except against oppressors"; first name Thomas) plus the ME2/ME3 record most relevant to a focus-and-resolve pitch: Cerberus rebuilding him from a corpse via the Lazarus Project (a direct mirror to Jack's own tank), Mordin's death at the Shroud finishing the genophage cure, and Thessia — the one fight where Kai Leng actually got the better of him and walked off with Vendetta, which Jack uses as the counter-example, not the insult. Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station, days earlier in the same push on Cerberus's headquarters, closes the speech as proof the focus she's asking for is already proven, not a new trick.
Second revision per Thomas, correcting two errors: (1) the outline had previously let the closing section cite the Illusive Man's suicide as settled proof Jack could point back to. That confrontation happens on the Citadel, concurrent with or immediately after the London conduit assault itself — part of the endgame this speech is walking Shepard out the door toward, not something resolved before it. It has been cut entirely; Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station (a distinct, already-resolved event from the assault on Cerberus's headquarters, which happened before this morning) carries that closing beat on its own. (2) the whole episode was misdated as the evening before, ending in the two of them going to sleep. It is corrected throughout to the morning of the assault itself: the fleet is already massed, the plan already briefed, nothing left to prepare — Jack is waking Shepard and getting him moving, not tucking him in. No section still ends on rest; every "tonight"/"tomorrow" reference has been changed to "today," "now," or "in the next hour," and "The Last Quiet Night" is renamed "The Last Quiet Hour" to hold the tattoo-and-sentiment beat inside a tense pre-launch hush instead of an evening of repose. The Crucible's final choice and Shepard's fate at the end of it remain deliberately left out: that hasn't happened yet either, and reaching for it would still be narrator omniscience, not something Jack could actually voice this morning.
This does not strain the form. `motivational`'s brief is explicit that "the narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it" — and Jack's whole method here is to make Shepard's history do exactly that work on Shepard himself: he's not telling her own story for its own sake, she's holding up his record as the evidence because a room full of only Jack's proof lets him nod along without it landing on him. Spine stays `mixed` — some sections anchor to Jack's own events/scenes, some to Shepard's, most to both at once, which is precisely what a speech that argues from the listener's own life looks like structurally. No change to form.

required_facts.fact: Jack, a human woman with a history of violence and unprecedented biotic power, has been held in cryostasis aboard the Purgatory, a notorious turian-operated prison ship. She is rumored to be the most powerful human biotic ever encountered, with a violent past that made her dangerous enough to require permanent cryo-imprisonment. Cerberus negotiates her release by paying an exorbitant fee to the turian operators. When Commander Shepard arrives at the prison to secure Jack's release, the turian Warden Kuril welcomes the Commander and gives a tour of the facilities while feigning cooperation. However, Kuril betrays Shepard over the facility's intercom, declaring that Shepard is too valuable to leave alive and ordering security forces to secure the Commander for a higher price. The prison erupts into chaos as security systems activate and rioting prisoners break free. Shepard fights through Blue Suns mercenaries, combat mechs (including FENRIS and YMIR variants), and rioting prisoners to reach the cryo-containment section. Upon release, Jack breaks her restraints and unleashes a massive biotic blast that destroys the four YMIR Mechs guarding her cell. She then smashes through a reinforced wall, triggering a series of catastrophic decompression events throughout the cellblock as Shepard pursues her toward an airlock. The Warden makes a final stand, armed with an M-76 Revenant and protected by a shield powered by three independent generators. Shepard must destroy each generator to bring down Kuril's shield, then neutralize the Warden. After Kuril's death, Jack reaches the airlock and eliminates the remaining guards. Upon boarding the Normandy SR-2, Jack becomes enraged at the sight of the Cerberus logo, her hatred of the organization boiling over. A batarian guard nearly assassinates her, but Shepard intervenes, shooting the attacker and proving her worth. Jack agrees to join Shepard in exchange for access to the Cerberus database aboard the Normandy to uncover the organization's secrets and find those responsible for her abuse. Her demands create conflict with Miranda Lawson and Jacob Taylor, both veteran Cerberus operatives. Jack takes up residence in the sub-deck below main engineering, establishing herself as a hostile presence until her loyalty is earned. As a consequence of releasing all prisoners to secure Jack, Shepard receives threatening communications from an escaped psychopath named Billy.

After Commander Shepard was killed in 2183 when a Collector cruiser destroyed the SSV Normandy SR-1 over Alchera, Cerberus recovered the body with Liara T'Soni's help and delivered it to the Illusive Man, who launched the Lazarus Project: a secret effort whose sole purpose was to bring Shepard back. Believing only Shepard could stop the coming Reaper harvest while the Council did nothing, the Illusive Man poured over four billion credits and two years of work into the project, operated by the Lazarus Cell under Miranda Lawson with her assistant Wilson at the Lazarus Research Station and Minuteman Station. The reconstruction used cybernetic implants to rebuild Shepard's skeleton, regrown skin, fluids to restart the organs and blood flow, and facial reconstruction; Shepard emerged having partly lost prior skills and talents. Miranda pressed to implant a control chip in Shepard's brain, but the Illusive Man refused, insisting Shepard be revived exactly as before, with no genetic or neural tampering - a claim later confirmed by Lazarus records recovered during the assault on Cronos Station. Cerberus also grew a secret clone of Shepard as a source of spare organs; it was never used during the revival. In 2185, with Shepard's neurological activity nearly restored, the Lazarus Station suffered a catastrophic security breakdown: its LOKI and YMIR security mechs, their IFF reprogrammed (Wilson was blamed, though he proved to be a traitor working for the Shadow Broker), turned on the personnel and killed most of the crew. Woken early and still incompletely reconstructed, Shepard armed up, fought through the hacked mechs, met and shot the wounded Wilson on Jacob Taylor's warning that Wilson was the saboteur, and escaped by shuttle with Miranda and Jacob during the mission Prologue: Awakening. A later Illusive Man report stated the compromised station was destroyed by remote detonation and a Cerberus team sent to erase any incriminating evidence.

beats.text: The Normandy docks at Purgatory, where Cerberus has paid for the release of the prisoner Jack. The turian station commander, Warden Kuril, welcomes Shepard, declines to take the squad's weapons, gives a short tour of Cellblock Two and its ejectable cells, then leaves to confirm the credit transfer.
At Outprocessing, Kuril betrays Shepard over the intercom — the Commander is too valuable to leave without a price tag — and activates the prison's defences.

Fighting through Blue Suns mercs, FENRIS and YMIR mechs, and rioting prisoners, Shepard reaches a security console and releases Jack from cryostasis. Jack breaks her restraints, destroys the four YMIR Mechs guarding her cell with a single biotic blast, and smashes a hole through the wall.
Kuril makes a final stand with an M-76 Revenant behind a shield fed by three generators. Shepard destroys the generators and kills him.
Jack reaches the airlock and kills the guards. Seeing the Cerberus logo on the Normandy sends her into a rage; a batarian guard moves to ambush her and Shepard shoots him in the head.

Jack agrees to join in exchange for access to Cerberus files aboard the ship; Miranda and Jacob object. Back on the Normandy she demands the files, takes an immediate dislike to Miranda — "the cheerleader" — and settles into the sub-deck below main engineering.
Because freeing Jack required releasing every prisoner, Shepard receives a threatening email from an escaped psychopath named Billy.

beats.text: Someone has blown up a Cerberus training facility, and the Illusive Man sends Kai Leng and the agent Rasa — a pairing Leng resents — to bring the culprit in. Leng says he will handle it and Rasa is only there to write up the aftermath. On arrival they spot Blue Suns ships in the hangar and realize the mercs are a containment crew in case the agents fail. The target is Jack.

They find Jack by the reactor, just after she has cut down a group of Blue Suns. Leng draws his sword and threatens her; her biotics knock him flat. He comes at her from above and behind instead; she senses him and hurls him further away. By the time he digs his stuck sword loose, the Blue Suns' krogan leader has clubbed Jack unconscious from behind and carried her off to be ransomed to the Illusive Man.

Leng calls the whole thing "a colossal waste of time." Rasa disagrees — at least the Illusive Man now knows what Subject Zero can do. On the shuttle out Leng blames Rasa for Jack's escape and warns her never to be assigned with him again.

evidence.text: The Blue Suns also own the maximum security prison Purgatory. The prison is run by Warden Kuril who claims that Purgatory is for "the good of the galactic community", despite the harsh methods used to maintain order, including carrying out torture, beatings and even murder (blowing prisoners out of airlocks as examples). Prisoners are also sold to vengeful victims/relatives or to groups with large enough finances, such as Cerberus. The Blue Suns have a substantial presence within the prison and have utilized several YMIR Mechs to act as heavy\-hitters in case a riot broke out. The prison is known to hold the most dangerous criminals in the galaxy. The Blue Suns agree to keep them imprisoned only if their home planets agree to continually pay for their incarceration. Failure to pay is grounds for releasing the inmate at an unknown time and place on their homeworld; considering inmates like Jack inhabit the prison, most worlds presumably pay. Shepard will travel to Purgatory to recruit Jack, who has been purchased by Cerberus from the Blue Suns. Early on, Warden Kuril betrays Shepard, attempting to imprison the Commander, who he states is more valuable as a prisoner than a customer, leading to a fight breaking out between Shepard's team and Kuril's Blue Suns, with Shepard eventually releasing the entire cell block in order to free Jack from cryo containment. This causes a full\-scale riot throughout the ship, with the Blue Suns attempting to restore control, kill Shepard and re\-capture Jack. They ultimately fail with Shepard killing Kuril and Jack joining the Commander’s crew. Cerberus then retracts the funds they paid. A news report reveals that the Purgatory was destroyed, with the Blue Suns losing yet another piece of influence.

evidence.text:
Warden Kuril was the turian warden of the Blue Suns prison ship Purgatory. Originally a law enforcement officer on Palaven, Kuril grew frustrated with criminals repeatedly escaping custody, so he left and joined the Blue Suns, conceiving the idea of holding prisoners in space where escape was impossible. He was one of the few "barefaced" turians seen in the series, and was voiced by Fred Tatasciore.

When Commander Shepard came aboard Purgatory to recruit the biotic prisoner Jack, Kuril gave Shepard a tour and directed the Commander to Outprocessing to collect Jack. When Shepard opened the door, Kuril revealed he had betrayed Cerberus and ordered his mercenaries to capture and hold Shepard for ransom. Shepard instead released Jack from cryo; the biotic went on a rampage that wrecked prison blocks as she fought her way out. Deciding Shepard was too much trouble, Kuril chose to kill the Commander. In the confrontation Shepard called him a "two-bit slaver," and Kuril shouted that everything he did was for the good of the galaxy. Despite being protected by three external shield generators, which had to be destroyed before he could be harmed, Kuril was killed by Shepard.

In combat Kuril was one of the few NPCs armed with the M-76 Revenant, which he fired accurately, especially on higher difficulties, though he had no offensive powers. He relied on strong armor and shields, Tech Armor that could fully restore his shields once (only after his armor was gone), the three external shield generators, and elevated cover with no approach path, forcing engagement strictly at range. The page recommends disruptor and overload effects against his shields, incineration against his armor, flashbang or inferno grenades to prevent his shield restore, and heavy weapons such as the M-490 Blackstorm or M-920 Cain to end the fight quickly, and advises clearing the waves of Blue Suns Troopers, Centurions and Commanders before destroying the generators.

evidence.text:
Purgatory was a maximum-security prison starship owned and run by the Blue Suns mercenary company, located in the Milky Way's Hourglass Nebula around Osun. Its facility administrator was Warden Kuril. It was where Commander Shepard could recruit Jack, a dangerous and highly unstable biotic, during the mission Dossier: The Convict.

Originally an "ark ship" built to carry agricultural animals, Purgatory was seized by the Blue Suns during a large-scale battle in the Skyllian Verge, then rebuilt over years into a prison for sapient inmates. Rumors held that the Blue Suns sold skilled or fit prisoners to batarian slavers. When media investigated the slaving claims, the Blue Suns turned the scandal into income: claiming full compliance with Citadel law, Purgatory's crew would land at ports announcing they could no longer afford to hold prisoners and would have to release them locally, prompting governments to grant massive discounts on fuel, food and repairs to make them leave, and some even paid to offload their own prisoners. The listed population was 4,350, though journalists estimated nearly three times that during overcrowding. The ship was minimally armed with GARDIAN defenses and relied on Blue Suns fighters. It held about 30 blocks of stacked, movable cells serviced by mechanized claws, with open-air communal showers and field-generator towers to separate fighting inmates. A fork in the walkways led to a supermax wing of criminals in cryogenic stasis, where Jack was held under guard by multiple YMIR Mechs.

On Shepard's arrival, Kuril said Cerberus had paid for Jack's release and directed Shepard to Outprocessing, where Shepard could intervene in the brutal interrogation of a prisoner called Bimmy. Kuril then betrayed Shepard over the intercom, declaring the Commander "worth more as a prisoner than a customer," and set the Blue Suns guards on the squad. Shepard fought through and released Jack, who went on a destructive rampage. By the time Shepard killed Kuril, the prison was falling apart from structural damage. Afterward the Council sent rescue ships for any survivors in escape pods.
evidence.for_key: the Purgatory prison ship and Warden Kuril's betrayal of Shepard

evidence.text: The Illusive Man initially provides Shepard with four dossiers regarding potential recruits: a salarian scientist, a mysterious vigilante called Archangel, a krogan warlord, and a powerful but psychotic biotic. The salarian, Mordin Solus, is found on Omega and is working to stop a plague engineered by the Collectors but distributed throughout Omega by the vorcha. The vigilante Archangel is also on Omega, holding out on his own in a battle against three mercenary gangs. After reaching Archangel's hideout, Shepard learns that Archangel is actually Garrus Vakarian, a former C\-Sec agent. Garrus is seriously injured while battling the mercenaries, and, although he is permanently disfigured, he survives and joins the team. The krogan warlord, Okeer, is found on Korlus attempting to create the perfect krogan through unethical genetic research. When the warlord is killed, he leaves his creation, Grunt, under the care of Shepard. The biotic, known as "Subject Zero", is revealed to be a human woman named Jack. Cerberus arranges for her to be purchased from the prison holding her; Shepard travels to the Purgatory prison ship. Once there, however, Shepard is betrayed by the warden as he attempts to capture Shepard for a bounty. Shepard manages to escape the trap and rescue Jack, who joins the team despite an initial distrust of Cerberus operatives.

evidence.text:
"Dossier: The Convict" was a Mass Effect 2 recruitment mission acquired after Freedom's Progress. The dossier described Jack (no last name known) as rumored to be the most powerful human biotic ever encountered, with a history of violence, held in cryostasis aboard the turian prison ship Purgatory, whose operators Cerberus had paid for the prisoner's release. On arrival, the turian station commander Warden Kuril welcomed Shepard, gave a tour of Cellblock Two, and left to confirm the credit transfer. At Outprocessing, Kuril betrayed Shepard over the intercom, declaring the Commander too valuable to leave without a price tag, and activated the prison's defenses.

Fighting through Blue Suns mercenaries, FENRIS and YMIR mechs, and rioting prisoners, Shepard reached a security console and released Jack from cryostasis. Jack broke her restraints, destroyed the four YMIR Mechs guarding her cell with a massive biotic blast, and smashed a hole through the wall, triggering a chase through decompressing cellblocks. Kuril, using an M-76 Revenant and protected by a shield powered by three generators, made a final stand; Shepard destroyed the generators and killed him, ending the mission.

Jack reached the airlock, killed the guards, and was enraged on seeing the Cerberus logo on the Normandy. A batarian guard nearly ambushed her before Shepard shot him. Jack agreed to join in exchange for access to Cerberus files aboard the ship; Miranda and Jacob objected. Back on the Normandy, Jack demanded the files and immediately developed a dislike for Miranda, whom she called "the cheerleader." She took up residence in the sub-deck below main engineering. Because all prisoners had to be released to free Jack, Shepard received a threatening email from an escaped psychopath named Billy. Rewards included element zero, credits, and Ablative VI (Damage Protection) and Synchronized Pulsar (Shotgun Damage) upgrades. The mission was written by Brian Kindregan.

evidence.text:
The Blue Suns were a "private security organization" that was in reality a ruthless, discreet, and expensive mercenary outfit operating in the Skyllian Verge. Members bore a blue sun tattoo, removed with acid wash during high-risk jobs. The group was mostly batarian, turian, and human, and used YMIR, FENRIS, and LOKI mechs. It was founded in 2160 by Zaeed Massani and Vido Santiago as a protection racket, Zaeed leading the men and Vido handling administration. A dispute over hiring batarians led to a 2165 power struggle in which Vido seized control and nearly killed Zaeed. Vido then hired batarians freely and installed Solem Dal'Serah as the public head of operations while remaining hidden as "Co-Executive Officer."

In Mass Effect: Revelation (2165), the Suns were hired by Edan Had'dah for the Sidon raid; Saren Arterius killed several, including Groto Ib-ba, during his investigation, and Suns under Skarr captured Kahlee Sanders before dying when an element zero refinery was destroyed. In Incursion (2183) a Suns–Collector exchange of humans on Omega was wiped out by Aria T'Loak. In Redemption the Suns recovered Commander Shepard's body from Alchera for the Shadow Broker but were ambushed by Liara T'Soni and Feron. In Foundation the Illusive Man hired Suns as a containment crew during Subject Zero's rampage.

In Mass Effect 2 (2185) Shepard repeatedly clashed with the Suns: they controlled Omega's Gozu District until the plague weakened their non-human members; they besieged Archangel (Garrus Vakarian) alongside Eclipse and Blood Pack under coordinator Tarak, aided by Sidonis's betrayal, and were destroyed with Tarak's gunship. The Suns ran the Purgatory prison under Warden Kuril, who betrayed Shepard during Jack's recruitment and was killed. Suns officer Jedore funded Okeer's krogan project on Korlus and killed him. On Zorya, Zaeed pursued Vido Santiago through a Blue Suns-controlled refinery. Other operations included Harkin's Citadel racket, Prothean dig-site raids on Joab and Kopis, and pirate raids via the MSV Strontium Mule and Sanctum base. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), with Aria's help Shepard secured the allegiance of the Citadel Blue Suns under Darner Vosque, who had been raiding C-Sec weapons shipments and targeting General Septimus Oraka.
evidence.for_key: the Purgatory prison ship and Warden Kuril's betrayal of Shepard

evidence.text: “I want to go to the center of the place, my cell. I want to deploy a big fucking bomb. And I want to watch from orbit when it goes.” *Main article: Jack: Subject Zero* After looking through her files, Jack wants to deploy a bomb at the Teltin facility on Pragia, where Cerberus conducted their experiments on her. Shepard takes Jack to the facility, unexpectedly encountering Blood Pack mercenaries. After fighting through the mercs, they find another test subject, Aresh. Aresh hired the mercs to restore the Teltin facility in exchange for salvage. Jack wants to kill him, but Shepard has the option to stop her. The two plant the bomb in Jack's cell, and use the shuttle to escape before detonation. If Miranda's loyalty mission has already been completed, once Shepard returns to the Normandy, Shepard will have to resolve a dispute between Jack and Miranda regarding the involvement of Cerberus in Jack's torture. Shepard can resolve the conflict without picking a side, in which case, both Jack and Miranda agree to put off their fight until after the mission with the Collectors is over. If Shepard sides with Miranda, then the Commander will lose Jack's loyalty, but has the opportunity to regain her loyalty in a later conversation. In addition, if Shepard was in a romance with Jack, and sided with Miranda, then Jack will break off the relationship and will refuse to rekindle it.

evidence.text: *For her gameplay attributes in Mass Effect 2, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 2\)\#Jack.* Eventually Jack was captured and imprisoned in the Blue Suns operated prison ship, Purgatory. During her time there, she was attacked by a group of guards and prisoners who raped her, despite her efforts at fighting back. Their victory was short\-lived however, as Jack personally murdered every one of her attackers as soon as she healed. The incident led the Warden, eager for the amount of credits Jack could bring him from Cerberus and other buyers, to lock Jack in cryostasis, for both her and others' safety until Shepard's team came to buy her freedom. The tortures of Jack's time as Subject Zero and her subsequent life experiences have rendered her a borderline psychopath, with an unpredictably violent nature and a severely antisocial personality. She has an innate lust for violence, claiming to experience "warm feelings during a fight" due to her physiological conditioning as a child at Teltin (by shocking her for hesitating and stimulating her with drugs whenever she attacked). She has a tendency to spout profanities constantly in conversation and is very easily provoked. Her body is covered head\-to\-toe in elaborate tattoos and scars, some being remnants of her experimentation, while others mark prisons, kills, and major events in her life. Having been used and abused so many times by people in her life, Jack refuses to trust anyone and is clearly both angered and confused by Shepard's attempts at conversation, being unable to determine what the Commander wants from her. Yet underneath all of this, she is still frightened and tormented by memories of her past and longs for some kind of closure. She joins Shepard's team in exchange for Cerberus files detailing her experimentation at Teltin, after which she asks the Commander to help her destroy the now abandoned facility with a "huge bomb", symbolically planting it directly in the cell that was the source of all her misery.

evidence.text:
Ben Hislop was a human mercenary and munitions master who appeared in Mass Effect: Evolution. He signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the turian bombardment of Shanxi's settlements during the First Contact War, and fought in the resistance on occupied Shanxi. Recruited into Jack Harper's prohumanity movement, he formed a mercenary trio with Jack and Eva Coré, conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and served as Jack's right-hand man.

On Shanxi, Ben's unit ambushed a turian patrol and he personally fought and captured the turian general Desolas Arterius with Jack's help. He wanted to execute Desolas but Jack kept the general alive for interrogation. On a mission to find the artifact Desolas sought, Ben antagonized him while Jack's scheme defeated the turian subordinates. Reaching the artifact inside a cave, Ben and Jack were ambushed by hooded figures revealed to be cyberized turians, which proved freakishly strong. When Ben touched the artifact to try to shut it off, he was electrocuted; Jack pried him free but was also affected, leaving both incapacitated. Desolas seized them and ordered Ben's body taken for study.

When Harper and Eva pursued Desolas to Illium, they found Ben alive but mutated into a synthetic form like the "meta-turians." He retained some sense of his identity but followed orders from Desolas and Saren, bringing the artifact, the Arca Monolith, to Palaven, where Desolas tried to replicate Harper's enhancement without creating mindless husks. The artifact commanded Ben to excavate a second artifact to accelerate the transformation. When Eva tried to haul Ben out and then to destroy the artifact, it commanded Ben to slam her head against a wall, killing her. Coming to his senses, a horrified Ben charged Desolas and rammed him into the artifact before he could shoot Harper; Saren tore Desolas away. Prolonged contact with the released energy instantly killed Ben, and his body was later vaporized when Saren ordered an orbital bombardment of the temple. Harper later included Ben's and Eva's names in his manifesto as he became the Illusive Man.

evidence.text: Jack, however, has also been busy and has reached the airlock. The guards try to stop her, but her biotics take them down before they have a chance to even raise their weapons. Apparently, the large ship out the window draws Jack's interest, but she spots the Cerberus logo on the Normandy's bow planes. That sends her into a fit, allowing a batarian guard to sneak up on her, but before the guard can do anything he gets a shot in the head from Shepard's pistol. Jack spins around, and a conversation begins. If you have Jacob and/or Miranda, there are a few interesting comments from Jack during the conversation. You can earn a few morality points based on your conversation options: Jack wants access to Cerberus files aboard the ship; Miranda and Jacob think it's a bad idea. You will respond that you'll give her access in the exact same tone regardless of whether you were being honest or bluffing. Either way, Jack deems the matter settled and badgers your team why they're still standing about. Back on the Normandy, Miranda formally introduces herself and her role to Jack regardless of whether she was on the mission or not. Jack demands immediate access to the files, and you can either give them to her right away or tell her to settle in first. Either decision results in the last morality points for the mission. From the get\-go Jack has developed a dislike for the "cheerleader" and will rub it in Miranda's face when you do something to support Jack's aims. Jack then leaves the briefing room to settle at the lowest point on the ship. In between missions and assignments you can find her down the stairs outside Main Engineering on Deck 4\.

evidence.text: The war was going badly for the humans, yet the General saw fit to arm and train a group of mercenaries to engage the turians. However, as the turians compromised the supply lines he gave the order to pull out of Shanxi and retreat to Arcturus Station. He was convinced the turians were looking for something on the planet aside from humans, but Command felt the world was a lost cause, and he realized few of his men had the heart to fight the invaders anymore. One of the mercenaries, Jack Harper, convinced him to give his team more time to find out what the turians wanted. Williams gave them a Mako for transport and the turian prisoner Jack captured before going to him. The stress of the job meant Williams would drink on the job. Weeks after the eventual cessation of hostilities, General Williams presided over a prisoner exchange at Arcturus Station. Jack and his teammate Eva Coré were captured during their Shanxi mission, and Williams now knew Jack's turian prisoner was a fellow General, Desolas Arterius, who was able to gain the upper hand on the mercenaries. Insults were traded by both sides, though Williams wondered what's up with the hooded bodyguards Desolas brought to the exchange. When Desolas realized Jack could understand the language he shared with the bodyguards, he tried to take the human back, though General Williams would have none of it and ordered them off Arcturus. Later in the med bay, Williams was impressed at Jack's vitals, though he offered his condolences to Jack for his teammate Ben Hislop died back on Shanxi. Following the Shanxi retreat the resulting Alliance counterattack drove off the turians from the planet, but the Alliance was now espousing peaceful coexistence with their new alien neighbors. The General disagreed with this course of action, and planned on resigning his command shortly, though he encouraged Jack to continue his investigation. Williams was awarded a personal shuttle for a battle sometime in his career, and he gave it over to Jack and Eva to help their mission. |  | ***“This mission just got a lot more complicated.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
A catalogue of dialogue unique to Jacob when he is in Shepard's squad in Mass Effect 2 (with some Mass Effect 3 lines), organized into location-triggered lines, "talk to squad mate" conversations, and spontaneous combat and ambient barks. A recurring thread is Jacob defending Cerberus and the Illusive Man, especially during Jack's loyalty mission, where he insists the Teltin facility "went rogue." Representative verbatim lines:

- Jacob, on the Collector Ship entering the massive pod chamber: "Earth... they're going after Earth."
- Jacob, on the Collector Ship when the Illusive Man's foreknowledge is revealed: "It doesn't make sense for Cerberus to sell us out. It just doesn't."
- Jacob, during Jack's loyalty mission on the container logs: "This is... unbelievable."
- Jacob, dying if he leads the second diversion squad in the Suicide Mission without secured loyalty: "There were too many, but I got them through. You guys finish up for me, all right?"
- Jacob, if Shepard destroys the Collector Base and he survives: it was a "hell of a way to tell the boss you're quitting," adding he wished he could have seen the Illusive Man's face.
- Jacob, using Pull: "Get over here!" (a nod to Scorpion from Mortal Kombat), also "Gravity is one mean mother, huh?"
- Jacob, using Barrier: "Throwing up a barrier!" / "Nothing can hurt me now!"
- Jacob, caught in friendly fire: "Get me out of your god-damn sights!"
- Jacob, hearing Jedore's canned PA orders on Korlus: "Who does that?"
- Jacob, on Jack's recruitment mission seeing a prisoner beaten: "Commander, you seein' this shit?"
- Jacob, if a female Shepard dumps him for Garrus: he calls the turian a "Cuttlebone."

Other tagged lines: confronting Ish on Omega about a past ambush and warning Shepard against helping him; on Horizon, dismissing Ashley/Kaidan's accusation as "typical Alliance attitude"; and, if brought to the Shadow Broker's base, the Broker notes his and Shepard's deaths would cripple Cerberus.

evidence.text: “I doubted you once Shepard, and I lost you. That's not happening again.” When Shepard visits Ashley in the hospital, she will call him out if he was in a prior relationship with her, but pursued another person while working with Cerberus. She is very judgmental of Miranda and Jack but seems more comfortable with the idea of Shepard and Tali being together, saying "Tali is like a little sister, I totally approve... not that you needed my approval." Though despite saying that, if Shepard hasn't built enough of a friendly rapport with her, Ashley does display signs of jealousy during the assault on the geth dreadnought if brought along with Tali, even making catty remarks towards her. If Shepard has remained faithful to Ashley, the conversations in the hospital are a lot more cheerful and less confrontational. The relationship progresses well if Shepard tries to be as friendly as possible and buys Ashley 'The Collected Alfred Tennyson' from the Sirta Supplies store. If Ashley is chosen to come aboard the Normandy, Shepard can start, or restart a relationship with her. Ashley does not talk a lot on the Normandy. Eventually, Ashley will send an email asking Shepard for help; Ashley is going to comfort her younger sister Sarah who has lost her husband and doesn't want to do it alone. If Shepard is comforting and respectful to Ashley, the relationship is cemented further. Later on, she sends another email asking Shepard to meet her on the Citadel. Ashley tells him how her dad would have liked Shepard. She apologizes for all that has happened between them and asks if they are "going somewhere". If Shepard reciprocates, they share a kiss together. Just before the assault on the Cerberus headquarters, she visits the Captain's Quarters and, unless directly turned down, she tries to comfort Shepard about all the people they've lost. She expresses how she felt lost herself and that it broke her heart when Shepard was dead. At long last, they admit their love for each other, then kiss and spend the night together. In a final conversation between her and Shepard on Earth, they reflect on how many times they've saved each other in the past. Shepard then recites from one of Tennyson's poems *The Charge of the Light Brigade*, a reference to how poetry has been used to convey their feelings throughout their relationship. Ashley grabs Shepard and tells him she doesn't want him to go and that she loves him. He gently replies that he loves her too and then says 'let's get it done, and go home'. In a breaking voice, Ashley responds "aye aye Captain." If Ashley is the love interest for Shepard, the last thing he will see will be an image of Ashley looking at him and warmly smiling. After the firing of the Crucible, she will be seen placing Shepard's name on the memorial wall, or, if the Reapers are destroyed and enough of the galaxy's forces have been mustered, she will smile and refrain from placing the plaque, and the Normandy is seen flying off.

evidence.text:
This page catalogues the armor and weapons available in the mobile game Mass Effect: Infiltrator, in which the Cerberus operative Randall Ezno buys gear from an in-game store using credits earned or redeemed through found Cerberus intel. Each armor set comprises a body piece and a helmet that offer separate bonuses and can be mixed and matched. Weapons are also bought from the store and improved through purchased upgrades. The turian protagonist of the bonus mission uses a fixed basic armor and weapon that cannot be changed or upgraded.

Four armor sets are described. Cerberus Assault Armour favors offense, granting +10% biotic damage with +10% weapon damage from its helmet, and each piece costs 2000 credits. Aegis Defensive Armour combines N7 vest plating with tungsten alloy, giving +10% health and +10% shield strength from the helmet. The Stealth Suit, used by covert special forces, cuts tactical cloak recharge by 10% and adds +10% headshot damage via the helmet. Infiltrator Armour, which Randall starts with, grants smaller +3% bonuses to melee damage, weapon damage, and shield strength across both pieces.

Weapons include the M-96 Mattock Auto (a fully automatic version of the classic rifle, Randall's starting assault rifle), the M-22 Eviscerator shotgun (which fires serrated metal edges and violates intergalactic weapons treaties), the M-29 Incisor burst-fire sniper rifle, and the M-333 Particle Beam. The M-333 is an experimental Cerberus radiation weapon reverse-engineered from Collector technology, effective against shields and barriers but weak against armor, handles like a heavy weapon that prevents sprinting, does not require pausing to cool when it overheats, changes beam color as it levels, and is the only weapon exclusive to Infiltrator. Each upgradeable weapon has five levels: level 1 is basic function, with subsequent tiers (Tungsten Jackets, Target Optics VI, Scram Rails, Antarctic Heatsinks, and equivalents) adding penetration, accuracy, damage, and cooling for costs from 500 up to 5000 credits. The M-37 Falcon is the fixed weapon of the turian bonus-mission protagonist, switching between assault rifle and shotgun modes, each with its own heat level; it cannot be upgraded and Randall cannot use it.

evidence.text: This page contained under ~150 words of real prose and covered cut, non-canon content. Batarian State Arms (BSA) was a hardware manufacturing company. Because the batarian government did not trust private industry to build its military hardware, BSA existed as a vast nationalized institution infamous for waste and corruption. It produced effective if unethical chemical weapons and a line of Nuclear, Chemical, and Biological (NBC) protective armor. In the first Mass Effect it was a hidden manufacturer whose equipment was fully functional in the game files but only reachable via the PC console or third-party software. Its lines included the Terminator assault rifles (sometimes accessible through the Bring Down the Sky PC DLC), the Executioner shotguns, the Judgement pistols, the Lightning Strike sniper rifles, and Partisan/Skirmish light, medium, and heavy armor. A separate Batarian State Arms shop appeared on the Citadel in Mass Effect 3.

evidence.text:
An optional N7 assignment in Mass Effect 3, unlocked after completing either Attican Traverse: Krogan Team or Tuchanka: Turian Platoon. Cerberus was attacking and abducting civilians on the human colony of Benning, in the Euler system of the Arcturus Stream. Shepard landed to protect civilians during their evacuation. The mission plays out on the multiplayer map Firebase Ghost, a tight urban environment of numbered prefab buildings.

Shepard's squad fought Cerberus light infantry, Assault Troopers, Combat Engineers, Centurions and Turrets, through the upper streets, then reached a group of civilians and defended them as they moved toward a landing pad for extraction. The civilians were invulnerable and sprinted forward in stages toward the shuttle while Cerberus focused fire on Shepard. Comm logs from Svetlana Alexandrov and other residents warned "don't trust Cerberus. They're taking people against their will," and urged people to run. On the map Shepard could recover the dog tag of Alliance Soldier Bilal Osoba, needed for the side mission Benning: Evidence.

After Shepard declared an all-clear and the civilians reached the landing zone, the mission ended when Shepard selected the shuttle. At debriefing, Admiral Hackett said a rogue Cerberus group might be behind the continued civilian attacks; the Alliance regained a foothold on Benning and retook the planet, and Shepard received the Arcturus First Division war asset (+5 Reputation, 20,000 credits, the Capacitor Helmet). A saved civilian, Jessica Frohm, later emailed Shepard thanking her and saying she found hope that her lost friends' memory lived on in her.

evidence.text:
"Miranda: The Prodigal" was Miranda Lawson's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, available after the Horizon mission and requiring Miranda in the squad. Miranda's estranged father was moving to abduct her sister Oriana, whom Miranda had taken as a baby and hidden on Illium to give her a normal life. On Illium, Miranda's asari contact Lanteia at the Eternity bar revealed that Miranda's trusted childhood friend Niket was arranging the transfer. Traveling to the Illium cargo terminal, the squad was ambushed by Eclipse mercenaries led by Captain Enyala, hired by Miranda's father, and fought through the cargo docks with an optional Renegade interrupt to kill the lead Eclipse Engineer.

At Dock 94, Miranda confronted Niket, who admitted he had sold her out because he believed Oriana deserved to know the truth. A Paragon interrupt could stop Miranda from shooting him; either way Enyala shot Niket dead, and Miranda biotically flung Enyala across the room, beginning a difficult final battle against Enyala, an asari Vanguard, a salarian Eclipse Operative and waves of mercenaries. Afterward Miranda watched Oriana with her adoptive family from a distance and could be persuaded to introduce herself or leave unseen. The mission secured Miranda's loyalty and her trust in Shepard, rewarded the Slam power, credits and element zero, and could trigger the confrontation with Jack aboard the Normandy if Jack's loyalty mission was already complete. If left uncompleted, Kai Leng mortally wounds Miranda on Horizon in Mass Effect 3. Completing it and convincing Miranda to speak to Oriana yields an email from Oriana titled "Guardian angels."

evidence.text: Once you return to the Normandy, you can approach Miranda for her account of the meeting she had with Oriana on Illium. Miranda says that Oriana’s family was shocked from learning the truth, but Oriana adjusted quickly to that knowledge. Miranda is happy to know that Oriana has a normal life and family, in contrast to her own upbringing. If Miranda was not convinced to reveal herself to Oriana, she is less upbeat, but still satisfied that Oriana's safety is assured. #### Confrontation with Jack *See also: Loyalty\#Confrontations* If you have already completed Jack's loyalty mission, you will automatically return to the Normandy on mission completion. Joker will page Shepard over the PA saying that Jack just went to have a talk with Miranda. When Shepard decides to handle it, Joker jokingly replies, “Take pictures.” Shepard arrives in Miranda’s office only to find Jack flinging a chair across the room and Shepard tells them both to knock it off. Jack is furious that Miranda will not admit to what Cerberus did to her was wrong. Unless you have enough Paragon or Renegade points, you cannot end this situation without alienating one or the other crew member. If you have enough points, then you earn the loyalty of both crew members and can continue any relationships that you have started. If you fail, then you will lose out on any relationships with either one and her loyalty, depending on whom you alienate. The amount of morality points required also varies during the course of the game, due to how Mass Effect 2's Charm/Intimidate system works. You need a high percentage of the Paragon or Renegade points obtainable from the areas that you've explored in order to pass the persuasion check; the amount of the meter that is filled in does not provide an accurate indication of whether Charm or Intimidate will be possible.

evidence.text: *For her gameplay attributes in Mass Effect 2, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 2\)\#Miranda Lawson.* After Cerberus gains possession of Commander Shepard's corpse, the Illusive Man selects Miranda to be the head of the Lazarus Cell and puts her in charge of the Lazarus Project. Over the course of two years, Miranda oversees the development and implementation of Cerberus' vast resources towards bringing Shepard back to life. When Shepard briefly wakes for the first time, Miranda is the first and last person seen by Shepard before falling back to sleep. At some point, the research base comes under attack by a saboteur. Miranda wakes Shepard over an intercom and guides the Commander to the base's last shuttle. Miranda takes Shepard to be briefed by the Illusive Man, but not before killing the traitor who instigated the attack. When Shepard goes to investigate the colony of Freedom's Progress, Miranda becomes a permanent squad member. Aboard the Normandy SR\-2 she functions as Shepard's second\-in\-command, but she also serves as a proxy for the Illusive Man, to whom she reports regularly. According to EDI, Miranda is the leading operative of the Lazarus Cell which is headquartered on the Normandy. Initially, Miranda expresses skepticism towards the level of importance the Illusive Man has placed on Shepard, especially since the Lazarus Project required a huge investment of Cerberus's resources and her own time. She also notes that she wanted to implant Shepard with a control device to regulate the Commander's actions, but the Illusive Man declined her suggestion. Soon after their mission gets underway, Miranda admits that the Illusive Man's estimation of Shepard's value to their cause was accurate. Unfortunately, Miranda still retains some of the insecurities that drove her from home; despite leading an illustrious career, Miranda doesn’t believe she’s truly earned her accomplishments. Because of her father's genetic tampering which gave her the innate advantage to succeed, she still feels like she's living under his shadow, and that her failures are the only thing she truly owns. Miranda admits this has made her somewhat jealous of Shepard, whose vast accomplishments can be credited to skill, talent, and drive.

evidence.text:
Jack's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, available after Horizon and written by Brian Kindregan. After Shepard gives Jack access to Cerberus files aboard the Normandy, Kelly Chambers relays that Jack wants to see Shepard in her "hidey hole" on the Engineering Deck. Jack asks Shepard to help her destroy the decommissioned Teltin facility on Pragia, in the Dakka system of the Nubian Expanse, where Cerberus experimented on her as a child. She wants to plant "a big fucking bomb" in her old cell and watch it detonate from orbit.

On arrival EDI detects thermal signatures inside the complex but none near the landing zone. Moving through the facility, Jack recognizes rooms and revisits memories: a skylit atrium where she first saw sunlight, a bloodstained arena where she was pitted against the other children and drugged as a reward for killing and shocked for hesitating, a cell block, and a two-way mirror outside her own cell where she used to bang on the glass while the other children ignored her. Security consoles reveal the staff had "gone rogue" from the Illusive Man's orders, that all subjects were expendable except Jack, that children were exposed to chemicals and freezing temperatures, and that the project planned to infiltrate the Alliance's Ascension Project; a final log shows Jack killing the distraught doctor during the riot. The team fights varren, Blood Pack vorcha and krogan mercenaries (including a Pyro and the krogan Kureck), hired by Aresh.

In Jack's cell, Shepard meets Aresh, a former test subject who recognized Jack and is trying to restart the facility so the experiments "must have been for something." Jack draws a pistol; Shepard can use Charm to spare him, Intimidate to have Jack kill him, or plain dialogue options with corresponding Paragon or Renegade interrupts. Shepard can then leave or stay while Jack walks the cell recounting memories of the window, bed, desk, and a bloodstain. On the shuttle back, Jack fumbles with the detonator, then presses it when Shepard nods, and the bomb destroys the facility.

Back on the Normandy, if Miranda's loyalty mission is complete, Jack confronts Miranda in her office, throwing a chair, furious that Miranda will not admit Cerberus was wrong. Without sufficient Paragon or Renegade standing, Shepard must alienate one crewmate, losing that person's loyalty and any romance (recoverable later). Cerberus Intel emails that the Illusive Man had ordered the project shut down before the riot, that arriving personnel found all guards and most subjects dead, and that surviving children were given amnesic treatments and delivered to the Alliance as "slaver attack" survivors. Rewards include 750 experience, 30,000 credits, 500 element zero, a Biotic Damage (Hyper-amp) upgrade, and Warp Ammo for Jack. If Aresh is spared, a Mass Effect 3 news alert reports he died saving a shuttle of children evacuating a Reaper-occupied colony; his full name is given as Aresh Aghdashloo.

evidence.text: Sometime after the assault on the Collector Base, Cerberus kidnapps former operative Paul Grayson, who had been working for Aria T'Loak on Omega. Operatives led by the Illusive Man's favored assassin, Kai Leng, attack Grayson's apartment, kidnapping Grayson and murdering his lover Liselle. Grayson is taken to one of Cerberus' many research stations, where the Illusive Man orders him implanted with recovered Reaper technology. Before Grayson had been kidnapped, however, he had sent all the information he had on Cerberus to Kahlee Sanders in the hope she could use it to bring down Cerberus or protect herself from harm. Sanders turns to Admiral David Anderson for assistance, who in turn seeks the help of the turians due to his concerns about Cerberus infiltration of the Alliance hierarchy. The turians launch raids against several Cerberus bases and front companies. A number of Cerberus agents and supporters are also arrested on the Citadel, greatly impairing the operations of the organization. The capture of two military training bases and four major research labs is estimated to cost the Illusive Man trillions of dollars in losses. Still believing that Cerberus needs to protect and defend humanity, and that the augmented Grayson, who had escaped Cerberus custody during the turian attack, is now a huge threat to Cerberus operations and to humanity itself, the Illusive Man makes a business deal with Aria T'Loak, asking her to kill Grayson in exchange for a substantial sum of money. The trap fails and Grayson escapes once more. Kai Leng, who had observed the failed ambush, offers to transport Sanders and Anderson off Omega, but they turn on him, overpowering him with the aid of a group of turian mercenaries, and use his ship to pursue Grayson to Jon Grissom Academy. Once they catch up with him, Kai Leng breaks free, eliminates Grayson, and escapes capture, albeit severely injured. The Illusive Man recontacts Aria, and is able to successfully negotiate the return of Cerberus data logs from Grayson's time in captivity. With all the "loose ends" tied up, the Illusive Man returns to the twin tasks of rebuilding his damaged organization and continuing preparations to combat the Reapers. |  | ***“Where the hell are these things coming from?”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Invasion** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: A short\-haired Rasa was accosted by Kai Leng for yet another mission in service to Cerberus. A training facility was under attack, and the Illusive Man dispatched them both to haul the perpetrator in for questioning. The target had biotics off the charts, as Rasa learned from the given dossier, and she doubted her purpose for being included when Leng declared he would be taking the operation seriously. In response, Leng told her she would be handling the aftermath analysis of events. A short time later at the training facility, Rasa took notice of the Blue Suns ships parked in the hangar. She did some further digging into the target and suspected that she was formerly of Cerberus, one of the biotic kids the organization trained in the early years. A mercenary contingent and two operatives for just one girl must mean Cerberus and the target were related, Rasa reasoned, as the agents continued to search for Jack. Soon enough Rasa and Leng found Jack just after she's done dealing with some Blue Suns soldiers. The Cerberus duo prepped their weapons but proved no match for Jack's biotic onslaught. More Blue Suns swarmed the scene, forcing Jack to make everything in the vicinity fly. Rasa begged the biotic to stop as she clung on one hand, but Jack was set on killing everyone. Subject Zero's rampage was only halted by a blow to the head. Rasa called out to the Blue Suns to clarify what they're doing when they started to haul Jack off, and one of their number responded that Jack would have to be ransomed by the Illusive Man. Rasa grudgingly accepted the situation as Kai Leng started to recover near her, remarking that the Illusive Man won't be happy with it. Leng thought the mission a waste of time, but Rasa was uncertain: at the very least, the Illusive Man will know Subject Zero's worth and capabilities.
